claude_only.name: Which authoritative identifier and version designate the exact model or system under evaluation?
Is the evaluated unit the bare model, a guarded endpoint, or the full deployed system including scaffolding and tools?
Which inference configuration, decoding parameters, system prompt, tooling and safety filters form part of the evaluated subject?
How is a hosted or continuously updated endpoint pinned so results remain attributable to a fixed subject?
What precise claim about capability, safety or quality is this evaluation designed to support or refute?
Which documented intended purpose, deployment context and affected populations bound the validity of the claim?
Which uses, populations, languages or environments are explicitly outside the evaluated claim?
What documented limits on generalisability apply outside the tested distribution?
Under which legal, regulatory, contractual or internal-policy basis is this evaluation required or commissioned?
Which event triggered this evaluation instance — release gate, capability threshold, incident, drift alarm or scheduled review?
Which decision or gate consumes the result, and who is accountable for that decision?
Which named organisations and roles designed, executed, scored and reviewed this evaluation?
What degree of independence separates the evaluators from the development team, and how is it evidenced?
What evidence establishes that assessors and human raters are competent for the domain and risk being measured?
Which conflicts of interest were declared and how were they managed?
Which method class is applied, and why is it appropriate to the property being assessed?
Which properties can this method class not evidence, and what complementary method covers that gap?
Against which baseline, reference implementation or comparator system are results interpreted?
How is the method shown to reflect the state of the art at the time of execution?
Which dataset version, snapshot or split identifiers, and which checksums, are bound to this evaluation?
How is ground truth or the reference answer defined, produced and quality-assured for each item?
What controls establish that the evaluation items were not present in training or tuning data?
How is a held-out or canary split protected from repeated exposure that would invalidate future results?
What is the exact computational definition, unit and aggregation rule for each reported metric?
Which construct does the metric claim to measure, and what evidence links the metric to that construct?
Which scorer implementation, version and configuration produced the metric values?
What rounding, significant-figure and tie-breaking conventions govern reported values?
Which factors must results be disaggregated by, and how was that factor list justified?
What minimum sample size per subgroup is required before a disaggregated result is reportable?
Which disparity comparison is applied across subgroups, and what gap is treated as a finding?
How are protected attributes obtained or inferred for disaggregation, and under which lawful basis?
Which acceptance thresholds and probabilistic criteria were fixed before results were observed, and where is that pre-registration recorded?
Who set each threshold, on what basis, and with what safety margin?
How is a change to a threshold after results are known authorised, justified and disclosed?
What consequence follows automatically from breaching each threshold?
How were raters recruited and how does the rater population relate to the affected population?
Which inter-rater agreement statistic is computed and what value is required for the result to be usable?
Which human-subject protections, consent arrangements and ethics approvals govern the evaluation?
How are raters blinded to system identity and condition to prevent expectancy effects?
Which threat model, attacker goals, capabilities and knowledge assumptions define this adversarial test?
Which attack classes — evasion, poisoning, privacy, prompt injection, misaligned output — are in and out of scope?
How much elicitation effort, tooling and time was expended, and how is that effort evidenced as sufficient?
What stopping rule ends the exercise, and how are unresolved attack avenues recorded?
Which identifier uniquely designates this run, and how does it relate to the campaign and to repeated epochs?
Which configuration values — seeds, sampling parameters, batch, concurrency, epochs, prompt template — are captured with the run?
What are the run start and end times, and how are they distinguished from result publication and record ingestion times?
What compute, token, latency, monetary and energy quantities are recorded for the run?
Which code revision, dependency versions, container image and hardware description are recorded for the run?
Which sources of non-determinism are permitted, and how are they bounded or seeded?
What exact procedure and inputs allow an independent party to replicate the run, and what tolerance defines success?
Which parts of the run are irreproducible, such as a retired endpoint or a one-off rater panel, and how is that recorded?
How is a single reported result value uniquely identified across subject, task, split, metric and factor?
What is the traceable path from per-item scores through reducers to each headline value?
Which fields are retained per evaluated item, and which are required to re-score without re-running inference?
When a result is recomputed or corrected, how are the prior value, the scorer version and the reason retained?
Which uncertainty estimate accompanies each headline value, and by what procedure was it computed?
How was the number of items and repetitions determined to be adequate for the claimed resolution?
Under which rule is a difference between two systems or two versions declared meaningful rather than noise?
How are multiple comparisons across metrics, factors and checkpoints controlled?
Which items constitute the sealed evidence package for this evaluation, and how is completeness asserted?
Which digest, signature or timestamping mechanism protects the package, and who holds the signing authority?
How is a later alteration of any packaged artefact detected and reported?
In what neutral form is the package transferred to an auditor or authority without loss of meaning?
Which generation, derivation, usage and attribution edges must be recorded between evaluation entities?
Which agent — person, organisation or software — is recorded as responsible for each activity and artefact?
How are activity start and end times recorded and reconciled with the time the record reached the evaluation store?
How is lineage preserved when datasets, models or scorers are governed in external systems?
How is a single finding identified and cited independently of the report that first presented it?
Which specific results, items and traces substantiate the finding?
Which severity and likelihood scale classifies the finding, and who assigns it?
What states can a finding occupy — open, accepted, mitigated, disputed, withdrawn — and what moves it between them?
Which threats to construct, internal and external validity are declared for this evaluation?
How is benchmark saturation, gaming or optimisation against the test set assessed and disclosed?
How are inconclusive or negative results recorded so they cannot be silently dropped?
How and when is the effectiveness of the measurement approach itself reviewed?
Who holds the authority to approve or reject on the basis of this evaluation, and under which delegation?
What decision was taken, on which sealed evidence version, and with what conditions attached?
Which deployment scope, markets, populations and time window does the authorisation cover?
On what documented basis may release proceed when an acceptance criterion is not met, and when does that waiver expire?
Which states does an evaluation instance pass through from planned to archived, and which transitions are irreversible?
Which changes to model, data, threat landscape, scaffolding or deployment context oblige re-evaluation?
At what cadence is periodic re-evaluation and in-production measurement required?
Under what conditions is a completed evaluation declared invalid, and how are dependent approvals affected?
Which audience tiers exist and what content is withheld or summarised in each?
How is it ensured that public claims never exceed what the full internal evidence supports?
How are report versions, corrections and retractions identified and communicated?
Which report content is mandated by regulation or code, and by what deadline?
What level of access — black-box, grey-box, weights, fine-tuning or internal tooling — is granted to external evaluators?
Which contractual terms bound scope, timing, safe harbour and publication rights?
On what basis may an external evaluation be omitted, and how is that basis evidenced?
How is disagreement between internal and external assessments recorded and resolved?
What is the default access rule for each record scope, and which roles hold read or write rights?
Which uplift-relevant or exploit-enabling details must be redacted, held separately, or shared only with authorities?
How are personal data in prompts, traces and rater records minimised, lawfully based and protected?
Which access events are logged, and for how long are those logs themselves retained?
What minimum and maximum retention period applies to each evaluation record class, and on what legal basis?
How are conflicts resolved between data-minimisation deletion duties and evidence-retention duties?
How is a legal hold applied, recorded and released across evaluation records?
What summary or digest must survive after primary records are deleted so that prior claims remain auditable?
Which external framework clauses does each evaluation record claim to address, and what evidence supports the claim?
How are alignment statements prevented from being read as certified conformance?
Which identifier schemes and namespaces are used for subjects, datasets, metrics and reports across organisations?
Under what conditions may results from two organisations or two rounds be compared without misleading readers?
Where two frameworks impose conflicting requirements, how is the conflict recorded and resolved?

grok_only.name: What authoritative master-system identifier does the evaluation platform of record assign to this campaign, and which governed IRI or Dimension UUID or ULID is used if the master system has none?
What is the evaluation goal in non-jargon terms, who will use the results, and what decision will the results change?

Is this campaign a standardized benchmark comparison, red-team or adversarial event, human or field test, conformity-assessment test, post-market monitor, or a composed TEVV-Athlon of several event types?
What is the campaign lifecycle state (planned, in execution, scored, synthesized, approved, superseded or withdrawn) and which event times mark each transition?
Which claims, trustworthiness characteristics or metrology blocks are under test, and how is each claim stated so a finding can be true, false or inconclusive?
What quantitative or qualitative acceptance thresholds, including uncertainty bounds, must be met for a pass, and who authorized those thresholds?
What go, no-go, waive or conditional-deploy rule will be applied to aggregated findings, and which residual risks remain acceptable if the rule fires?
Must accuracy or other performance levels be declared in instructions for use or technical documentation, and which metrics are the declared ones?
Which model or AI-system artifact identifier, version and interface (API, checkpoint, agent bridge) is the subject under evaluation?
What generation, decoding, tool-use, temperature and context-window configuration was frozen for this campaign so results are attributable to the subject rather than to an uncontrolled adapter?
Were the actors who built or operate the subject separated from the actors who designed, executed or scored the evaluation, and if not what conflict is recorded?
Is the subject open-weight, limited-access API or closed, and how does that access class constrain reproducibility and third-party re-run rights?
Which dataset master identifier, version, split and Croissant or equivalent description is bound as the evaluation set, and is that binding a test split rather than training data?
What is the target or ground-truth field, who authored the labels, and what annotation protocol or inter-rater evidence supports those labels?
What license and usage restrictions apply to evaluation-time use, redistribution of prompts or publication of sample-level outputs?
Is the bound dataset live or frozen, and if live how is the exact snapshot used by a run identified?
What controls prevent training-set overlap, prompt leakage, canary exposure or use of the test split during development of the subject?
How was the sample frame shown to be representative of the intended operational domain, and which groups or languages are known to be missing?
Were transcripts or items scanned for evaluation awareness, memorization of test items or harness artifacts, and what was the outcome?
Where expected results are unavailable or non-deterministic, how is the test oracle defined so pass and fail remain decidable?
What is the exact metric definition, unit, aggregation (micro, macro, weighted, sample-mean, clustered) and direction of goodness?

Which metrics are measured on the same scenario so accuracy is not the sole reported desideratum, and which HELM-class metrics (calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity, efficiency) are absent?
What construct-validation argument shows that this metric measures the intended trustworthiness characteristic rather than a Goodhart proxy?
What statistical test, confidence interval or clustered-error method will be used to compare systems or detect change, and is the analysis pre-registered?
What task, domain, language or modality, and user-facing use case define this scenario, and which HELM or Inspect eval identifier does it correspond to?
What adaptation protocol (zero-shot, few-shot, chain-of-thought, agent loop, tool use) is frozen, including prompt templates and in-context example policy?
If the task is agentic, which tools, MCP servers and sandbox (Docker, Kubernetes or other) isolate untrusted model actions, and what approval gates exist for tool calls?
Does the scenario depend on a geographic, legal or language locale, and if so which locale constraints apply to items and raters?
What master-system run identifier, log URI and status (started, success, error, aborted, retried) identify this execution?
When did the run start and end as event time, and when was the log ingested, each in RFC 3339 with seconds and offset?
What evaluation environment, hardware, software versions, seeds, parallelism, epoch count and cost or energy envelope were used?
Which error-handling, sample limits, timeouts or early-stopping rules fired, and is the result a partial run?
Which scorer or judge configuration produced each sample score, including grader model, rubric, and whether scoring was live or deferred and later re-scored?
For each sample, what were the input, output, target, score value, explanation and refusal or scanner flags?
If a model or crowd judge was used, what agreement with gold oracles, inter-rater reliability and bias controls support treating those judgments as evidence?
Do sample inputs, outputs or rater notes contain personal data or prohibited content, and what minimization or redaction applies?
What aggregate metric values were obtained for each metric and subgroup slice, including sample size and missingness?
What interval, standard error or significance-test result accompanies each aggregate, and against which baseline or champion was the comparison made?
Which metric trade-offs (for example accuracy versus robustness or toxicity) are material, and were they measured in the same scenario?
Is this result set draft, final, corrected or retracted, and what errata supersede earlier published numbers?
For each claim, is the verdict support, refute or inconclusive, and which result rows and sample exhibits constitute the evidence?
What limitations, missing scenarios, distribution shift and construct gaps must be disclosed with the finding?
Who authored, reviewed and approved the finding, and from which run logs was it derived?
If the finding arises from red-team or adversarial events, is publication restricted because it discloses exploitable vulnerabilities?
Was the gate outcome go, no-go, conditional deploy or waive, against which claims and findings, and what conditions attach?
Which role or notified body had authority to decide, and was a third-party or internal-control procedure used?
When was the decision made as event time, and when was it recorded in the register as observation time?
Which evaluation logs, metric declarations and technical-documentation excerpts were in the evidence pack at decision time?
Which events (subject version change, data drift, incident, scheduled cadence, threshold breach, regulatory request) trigger a new campaign or run?
If the system continues to learn after deployment, what evaluation detects biased feedback loops and what mitigation is required before continued operation?
Has a market-surveillance authority, AI Office or scientific panel requested or conducted an evaluation of this subject, and what access was granted?
What post-market monitoring plan identifiers, metrics and reporting frequency apply to this deployed subject?
Who may read campaign metadata, sample-level logs, red-team findings and approval records, and which default-deny exceptions exist?
What retention period, legal hold and deletion or redaction method apply to logs, rater data and personal data in samples?
What pinned dataset hashes, subject versions, task specs, seeds and scorer versions are required to re-run, and which of those cannot be released because the subject is closed?
How is integrity of the run log and any post-eval score or tag edits guaranteed, including hashes, etags and provenance of log updates?
Which party owns the evaluation records and which accountable deployer must be able to produce them to an authority?

requirements: Resolve every provider-only bundle, layer and finding against primary evidence.
Resolve the model boundary and entry kind before accepting structure.
Verify live URLs and version pins for all accepted sources.
Record every rejected and deferred node with a reason.
Do not publish while any critical conflict remains unresolved.
